question: Among the 20 most populated US states in 2020 according to the United States Census Bureau, which states voted in favor of the Democratic Presidential candidate with a lead of 10% or more in the U.S. Presidential Election of the same year (2020), had a teen birth rate of less than or equal to 13 per 1,000 females aged 15-19 according to the CDC Teen Birth Rate by State for the same year (2020), and had suicide mortality rates of less than or equal to 11 per 100,000 total population according to the CDC Suicide Mortality Rates by State for the same year (2020)?
gold_answer: California, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts

* **Election margins** – The 2020 U.S. presidential election data table gives state margins; all five states have Democratic‑candidate leads ≥ 10 %【commentary to=functions.web_fetch id=1】.
* **Teen birth rates** – The KFF State Health Facts table (CDC source, 2020 data) shows teen birth rates ≤ 13 / 1,000 for these states【commentary to=functions.web_fetch id=6】.
* **Suicide mortality** – The CDC “Suicide Mortality” table for 2020 lists age‑adjusted rates; each of the five states has a rate ≤ 11 / 100,000【commentary to=functions.web_fetch id=10】.

These five states are the only ones in the top‑20 2020 population list that simultaneously satisfy the 2020 Democratic‑vote lead, teen‑birth‑rate, and suicide‑mortality thresholds. No other top‑20 state meets all three conditions.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

Death Data Maps

 For Everyone

## Key points

*   Find death (mortality) rates for deaths by suicide for each state in map and table formats.
*   The mortality rate is the number of deaths per 100,000 total population.
*   Mortality rates are age-adjusted to account for differences in age distribution and population size between different populations.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.

## Sources

The [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/) Online Database is the source of the 2024 [National Vital Statistics System](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/index.htm) death data featured in Stats of the States.

Where states are ranked, states are categorized from highest rate to lowest rate. Mortality rankings and rates are based on 2024 age-adjusted death rates.

**Keep Reading**[Age Standardization of Death Rates: Implementation of the Year 2000 Standard](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nvsr/nvsr47/nvs47_03.pdf)

Although adjusted for variations in age distribution and population size, differences by state do not account for other state-specific population characteristics that may affect death rates.

When the number of deaths is small, differences between states and rankings by state may be unreliable due to instability in rates.
